investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II)
investigations.sample_dimensions_summary: Clear 9.525 mm diameter (4.7625 mm radius) PMMA rods (e.g., sample 218m in O15a/O15b) and 6.35 mm cohort rods inside 7.6 cm x 7.6 cm MSG flow duct.
investigations.shared_hardware_context: Conducted inside the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) 7.6 cm x 7.6 cm flow duct.
investigations.methods: Burned cylindrical PMMA rods under controlled concurrent and opposed forced airflows in ISS microgravity using fixed, changing, and staged fan protocols. NTRS 20150008961 reports the 24-test ISS concurrent-flow cohort and separate short drop-tower tests.
investigations.limitations: Table A.5 run matrix leaves run-level pressure unreported (nominal ISS cabin is ~101.3 kPa). Candidate tests O15a and O15b shared physical sample 218m (repeated-burn history) and experienced flow changes during the tests. Short drop-tower companion tests must not be pooled with ISS runs.

research_lead.question: How does step-down or changing ventilation airflow alter solid acrylic (PMMA) flame survival and extinction in spacecraft microgravity?
research_lead.finding: In concurrent-flow PMMA rod burns, high forced airflow can induce blowoff whereas stepping airflow down as oxygen depletes (from 14.8% initially to 13.6% finally in Figure 6.4, and across candidate tests O15a/O15b on sample 218m) leads to radiative quenching.
research_lead.conditions: ISS microgravity (MSG flow duct), clear 9.525 mm diameter PMMA rod (sample 218m) and 24-run cohort, 13.6%–21.0% O2, forced flow 0.5–45.0 cm/s.
research_lead.limitation: Does not test partial lunar gravity (~1/6 g) or the 34% O2 / 56.5 kPa exploration cabin atmosphere.

investigations.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment - I (Saffire-I)
investigations.sample_dimensions_summary: 0.4 m wide x 0.94 m long SIBAL (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass) fabric panel in uncrewed Cygnus vehicle.
investigations.shared_hardware_context: Flown aboard an uncrewed Cygnus resupply vehicle after ISS departure.
investigations.methods: Ignited a large 0.4 m x 0.94 m SIBAL (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass) fabric panel in a full-scale spacecraft module enclosure under 20 cm/s ventilation flow.
investigations.limitations: Tested thin cotton-fiberglass fabric in normal-air equivalent (~21% O2, ~101 kPa) in microgravity; did not test thick PMMA rods or 34% O2 / 56.5 kPa lunar rover conditions.

research_lead.question: How does a meter-scale solid fabric fire grow and interact with spacecraft enclosure volume in microgravity compared to small glovebox samples?
research_lead.finding: Saffire-I demonstrated steady concurrent flame spread across a 0.4 m x 0.94 m SIBAL fabric sample at 20 cm/s airflow in Cygnus (DOI 10.60555/0t15-1z43), quantifying large-scale flame spread and enclosure pressure rise.
research_lead.conditions: Uncrewed Cygnus microgravity, 0.4 m x 0.94 m SIBAL cotton-fiberglass sheet, ~21% O2, ~101.3 kPa, 20 cm/s airflow.
research_lead.limitation: Single atmosphere (~21% O2, 101 kPa) in orbital microgravity; not directly transferable to 1/6 g partial gravity.

investigations.title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight (SAME-R)
investigations.sample_dimensions_summary: Small cylindrical polymer and wire-insulation pyrolysis coupons in MSG smoke aging duct.
investigations.shared_hardware_context: Conducted inside the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox using thermal pyrolysis of spacecraft materials.
investigations.methods: Generated smoke aerosols from overheated spacecraft materials (including PMMA, cellulose/cotton, silicone, Kapton, and Teflon) and measured particle diameter distributions and aging for ionization and photoelectric detector calibration.
investigations.limitations: Focused on non-flaming oxidative pyrolysis smoke particle size distributions rather than open-flame quenching or blowoff boundaries.

research_lead.question: How do microgravity smoke particle size distributions from overheated spacecraft polymers affect early fire detector selection?
research_lead.finding: Microgravity lack of buoyancy increases residence time inside the hot zone, producing larger aggregated smoke particles than 1 g tests and shifting optical vs. ionization detector response sensitivities.
research_lead.conditions: ISS microgravity (MSG), thermal pyrolysis of PMMA, cotton, Kapton, silicone, Teflon at ~101 kPa.
research_lead.limitation: Measures smoke aerosol properties from pyrolysis rather than flaming extinction limits.

investigations.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
investigations.sample_dimensions_summary: Isolated 2–5 mm diameter liquid heptane and methanol fuel droplets in CIR/MDCA chamber.
investigations.shared_hardware_context: Conducted inside the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA).
investigations.methods: Dispensed isolated liquid fuel droplets (heptane, methanol) in quiescent and low-flow atmospheres diluted with inert suppressant gases (N2, CO2, He, Xe) to quantify minimum extinguishing concentrations and radiative quenching.
investigations.limitations: Liquid droplet proxy experiment (heptane/methanol); droplet burning rates and gas-dilution extinction concentrations cannot be directly pooled with solid PMMA rod flammability.

research_lead.question: How do inert gas diluents (CO2, N2, He) extinguish spherical microgravity flames, and when do post-extinction cool flames persist?
research_lead.finding: FLEX mapped droplet burning rates and radiative/diffusive extinction limits across oxygen and diluent concentrations, revealing second-stage low-temperature cool-flame burning in alkane droplets after visible flame quenching.
research_lead.conditions: ISS CIR/MDCA microgravity, isolated heptane and methanol droplets, 15%–25% O2, 70–300 kPa.
research_lead.limitation: Proxy liquid droplet geometry; does not measure solid polymer surface regression or melt-layer dripping.

investigations.title: Lunar Gravity Combustion Investigation (LUCI)
investigations.sample_dimensions_summary: 4 mm diameter (2 mm radius) acrylic (PMMA) rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric burned at the same time in a shared rotating New Shepard sounding-rocket payload chamber.
investigations.shared_hardware_context: Flown aboard a rotating Blue Origin New Shepard sounding rocket simulating ~1/6 g; both the 4 mm acrylic rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric burned simultaneously inside the same chamber, so oxygen readings apply at shared-chamber scope.
investigations.methods: Simulated lunar gravity (~1/6 Earth g) aboard a rotating New Shepard sounding rocket in normal-pressure air (21% O2, ~101.3 kPa), burning a 4 mm diameter acrylic rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric at the same time.
investigations.limitations: Conducted in normal-pressure air (21% O2, 101.3 kPa) rather than the 34% O2 / 56.5 kPa exploration atmosphere, and burned both the 4 mm acrylic rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric simultaneously in the same shared chamber. Represented as a published_reference card pending run-level telemetry release.

research_lead.question: How does simulated lunar partial gravity (~1/6 g) aboard a rotating sounding rocket affect solid acrylic and fabric combustion compared to orbital microgravity?
research_lead.finding: LUCI (NTRS 20250010653) demonstrated simultaneous burning of a 4 mm acrylic rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric under ~1/6 g simulated by a rotating New Shepard sounding rocket in normal-pressure air, providing a partial-gravity anchor point distinct from 0 g ISS tests.
research_lead.conditions: Rotating New Shepard sounding rocket (~1/6 g), 21.0% O2, 101.3 kPa normal-pressure air, shared chamber with 4 mm PMMA rod + cotton-fiberglass fabric.
research_lead.limitation: Does not cover the 34% O2, 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa) lunar rover exploration atmosphere; oxygen readings are at shared-chamber level.

evidence.locator_detail: Appendix A, Olson Table A.5, Row O15a (printed pp. 110–111), Sample 218m (clear 9.525 mm PMMA rod)
evidence.reviewed_fact: Candidate test O15a in Olson Table A.5 burned clear 9.525 mm diameter (4.7625 mm radius) PMMA rod sample 218m under concurrent flow that changed during the test (15.6% initial O2, 15.2% final O2, calibrated flow 3.0 cm/s), ending in quenching with run-level pressure unreported.

evidence.locator_detail: Appendix A, Olson Table A.5, Row O15b (printed pp. 110–111), Sample 218m (clear 9.525 mm PMMA rod)
evidence.reviewed_fact: Candidate test O15b in Olson Table A.5 re-burned the same physical sample 218m (clear 9.525 mm PMMA rod) with changing flow during the test (15.2% initial O2, 14.9% final O2, calibrated flow 1.5 cm/s), ending in quenching with run-level pressure unreported.

evidence.locator_detail: Section 6.1, Figure 6.4 Staged-Flow PMMA Sequence (printed pp. 69–71)
evidence.reviewed_fact: In BASS-II Figure 6.4, airflow was reduced in steps and oxygen went from 14.8% initially to 13.6% finally; intermediate oxygen values, elapsed times, and unverified stage velocities remain null until reconciled with a specific run ID.
At the end of the staged airflow reduction in BASS-II Figure 6.4, oxygen concentration reached 13.6%.

evidence.locator_detail: NTRS 20150008961, Section 2 & Table 1: 24-Test ISS Concurrent-Flow PMMA Cohort and Companion Drop-Tower Tests
evidence.reviewed_fact: NTRS 20150008961 defines the 24-test ISS concurrent-flow PMMA rod cohort distinguishing low-flow radiative quenching from high-flow blowoff, alongside separate short drop-tower tests.

evidence.locator_detail: PSI-98 (DOI 10.60555/0t15-1z43) Investigation Summary & Cygnus Enclosure Telemetry
evidence.reviewed_fact: Saffire-I burned a large 0.4 m x 0.94 m SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric sheet aboard uncrewed Cygnus at 20 cm/s airflow in ~21% O2, ~101.3 kPa.

evidence.locator_detail: PSI-101 (DOI 10.60555/2np7-jv14) Final Report, Section 3 Smoke Particle Size Distributions
evidence.reviewed_fact: SAME-R measured moment-average smoke particle diameters and aging from overheated spacecraft materials (PMMA, cotton, Kapton, silicone, Teflon) in ISS microgravity.

evidence.locator_detail: PSI-69 (DOI 10.60555/mbq8-0451) FLEX Droplet Run Summary Table
evidence.reviewed_fact: FLEX quantified inert-gas dilution suppression and cool-flame behavior for isolated heptane and methanol fuel droplets in microgravity (15%–25% O2, 70–300 kPa).

evidence.locator_detail: NTRS 20250010653, Rotating New Shepard Sounding Rocket Flight Experiment
evidence.reviewed_fact: LUCI burned a 4 mm diameter acrylic (PMMA) rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric simultaneously in normal-pressure air (21.0% O2, 101.3 kPa) aboard a rotating Blue Origin New Shepard sounding rocket simulating lunar gravity (~1/6 g); oxygen readings apply at shared-chamber level.

evidence.locator_detail: NTRS 20240003211, Table 1 Recommended Crewed Lunar Exploration Atmosphere (8.2 psia, 34% O2)
evidence.reviewed_fact: NASA recommends a cabin exploration atmosphere assumption of 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa) total pressure and 34% oxygen for lunar surface rovers and habitats.

evidence.locator_detail: NTRS 20240003211, Table 1 Recommended Crewed Lunar Exploration Oxygen Concentration (34% O2)
evidence.reviewed_fact: The recommended exploration atmosphere specifies 34% oxygen by volume at 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa) total cabin pressure.

evidence.locator_detail: Section 4, Partial-Gravity Flammability Minimum & Buoyant Convection Crossover
evidence.reviewed_fact: Flammability limits in partial gravity (such as lunar 1/6 g) can extend beyond both microgravity and 1 g boundaries because moderate buoyant convection supplies oxidizer faster than 0 g diffusion without imposing 1 g blowoff strain.

exclusions.candidate_row_ref: NTRS 20150008961 24-Run Concurrent-Flow PMMA Cohort (22 Remaining ISS Runs & Short Drop-Tower Companion Runs)
exclusions.reason: While NTRS 20150008961 reports 24 ISS concurrent-flow PMMA tests and separate short drop-tower tests, only candidate rows O15a and O15b from Olson Table A.5 (NASA/TM-20210011385) have been individually cross-referenced in the initial reviewed run slice.
exclusions.resolution_rule: Keep published_run_count = 24 at the BASS-II study level and admit additional individual cohort runs into data/runs.csv only after two reviewers reconcile each original NASA run ID, calibration ID, and outcome against Table A.5 and PSI-25.

exclusions.candidate_row_ref: NASA/TM-20210011385 Section 6.1, Figure 6.4 Intermediate Stage Velocities and Elapsed Timestamps
exclusions.reason: Section 6.1 prose explicitly reports initial oxygen (14.8%) and final oxygen (13.6%) across the stepped-down airflow sequence, but intermediate stage oxygen percentages, exact step velocities, and elapsed times are not tabulated with exact numeric precision in the figure caption.
exclusions.resolution_rule: Ingest Figure 6.4 with 14.8% initial O2 and 13.6% final O2 while preserving explicit nulls for intermediate oxygen, elapsed_time_s, and airflow_cm_s, and keep run_id null until the underlying Table A.5 run ID is confirmed.

exclusions.candidate_row_ref: NTRS 20250010653 LUCI Sounding Rocket Shared-Chamber Burn
exclusions.reason: LUCI burned a 4 mm acrylic rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric at the same time in a rotating New Shepard sounding rocket chamber; oxygen readings apply to the shared chamber rather than an isolated single-sample duct run.
exclusions.resolution_rule: Model LUCI as a published_reference investigation card with shared_chamber scope rather than pooling it as an isolated run row in data/runs.csv.
